content.comment_body: I'm still experiencing the same issue when deploying [product_name] on AWS. I followed the steps suggested by [user_name] but this is with a newer version of AWS. Is there any update?

Hello [user_name], Could you please provide more details about your problem and your complete process? For example, which [article_no] your device uses, what you tried, where you encountered issues, and what your goal is. With the limited information provided in this topic and others, it's difficult for anyone to assist you effectively.

I'm attempting to deploy the [product_name] page to the AWS cloud. I set up the AWS IoT object, and data communication works properly. Deployment of the [product_name] project to AWS completes, and a new environment is created. I added an IAM role called "aws-elasticbeanstalk-service-role," which is required by this environment. However, when accessing the environment link, I encounter this message: HTTP Status 500 – Internal Server Error Type: Exception Report Message: Servlet.init() for servlet [springMvc] threw exception Description: The server faced an unexpected condition that prevented fulfillment of the request.

I've received a workaround from development for the 'HTTP Status 500 – Internal Server Error' issue with [product_name] [version_no] and AWS. A document is attached here for reference. [company_name] Support

Hi all, I wanted to share solutions for two errors I encountered while running my [product_name] application on AWS Elastic Beanstalk. Problem 1: "The instance profile aws-elasticbeanstalk-ec2-role associated with the environment does not exist." Go to IAM Console > Roles > Create role. Select "AWS service" then "EC2". Attach these policies: AWSElasticBeanstalkWebTier, AWSElasticBeanstalkWorkerTier, AWSElasticBeanstalkMulticontainerDocker. Name the role: aws-elasticbeanstalk-ec2-role. Problem 2: "Unable to assume role aws-elasticbeanstalk-service-role." (Environment stuck in Warning/Pending) Go to IAM Console > Roles > Create role. Select "AWS service" then "Elastic Beanstalk" (choose the Environment management use case). Ensure the AWSElasticBeanstalkService policy (or automatically selected policies, such as AWSElasticBeanstalkEnhancedHealth and [BINARY_DATA_REMOVED]) are attached. Name the role: aws-elasticbeanstalk-service-role. Hopefully, these tips help others save time.
